question.text: Lotus Growth Fund (Category II AIF) owns 15% of Zephyr Logistics, an unlisted company. Zephyr's FY25 EBITDA is INR 40 crore. Peer-set trading EV/EBITDA is 12x. Zephyr's net debt is INR 80 crore. Using the relative valuation approach with no illiquidity discount applied, what is the fair value of Lotus's stake in Zephyr?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 379), relative valuation produces enterprise value and the bridge to equity value requires deducting outstanding debt. EV = 12 x INR 40 crore EBITDA = INR 480 crore. Equity Value = EV - Net Debt = 480 - 80 = INR 400 crore. Lotus's 15% stake = 0.15 x 400 = INR 60 crore. The Trap: INR 72 crore applies 15% directly to EV and forgets to deduct debt. INR 48 crore is EBITDA x multiple x stake without using the EV bridge. INR 54 crore adds back cash incorrectly to the equity value. Note: The EV-to-equity bridge with debt deduction is on page 379; page 386 supports the multiples approach and notes that an illiquidity discount is typically applied for unlisted stock when relevant.
